<!-- custom-release-notes:start -->
# Retention manifests: a misnamed `.json` file no longer disables its claim silently

## What

`.swarm/retention.d/` previously skipped any `.json` file whose name fell outside
the manifest name grammar (for example `_reviewer.json`, `my reviewer.json`), with
no error: its claimed directory was then pruned at the default 30-day horizon, and
a malformed body in such a file did not refuse the unclaimed-directory catch-all as
documented.

A non-dot `.json` file in `retention.d` whose name is not a valid manifest name now
makes the unclaimed-directory catch-all refuse to run, with the file and the reason
in the sweep result, like any other malformed manifest. This includes a `.json`
name followed by trailing dots or whitespace (`reviewer.json `, `reviewer.json.`),
and the check is case-insensitive (`_x.JSON` is refused). Dotfiles and names that do
not end in `.json` (editor scratch files, `x.json.bak`) are still ignored.

## Behavior change: only the catch-all is refused

A malformed or misnamed manifest now skips only the tier-3 unclaimed-directory
catch-all (its `retention.dry_run` listing included). Every directory-family pass
and the other retention passes still run, because they never read the claims. This
narrows the v7.204.10 behavior, where an unusable manifest refused the whole sweep
and stopped family prunes as well. The catch-all stays fail-closed: nothing under
`.swarm/` that is unclaimed is deleted while a claim cannot be verified.

The reason is visible only in the debug log (`OPENCODE_SWARM_DEBUG=1`), because
neither production caller reads the sweep result. A grammar-valid stray `.json`
(for example `notes.json` or `owner-copy.json`) already refused this way before
this change; the change widens the set of names that do. OS file-manager duplicates
such as `owner (1).json` or `Copy of owner.json` used to be skipped harmlessly and
now stop the catch-all until renamed or removed.

## Migration

If a project has a hand-made `retention.d/_x.json` (or a name with a space or
non-ASCII letter, or a file-manager duplicate), rename it to start with a letter or
digit and use only letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, or delete it if it is not a
claim. Until then the catch-all is skipped, the file is named in the debug log
(`OPENCODE_SWARM_DEBUG=1`), and no unclaimed directory is deleted.

Doc corrections to the v7.204.10 release notes (#3727), which stay as published:
the tier-3 rule is "no future-dated file" (age is measured from regular files),
not "no future-dated entries", and the retention result is surfaced only in the
debug log because neither production caller reads it.

---

fix(delegation-gate): the completion gate no longer wedges OpenCode v2 Code Mode sessions

- On an OpenCode v2 host every plugin tool is reached through the host-owned
  Code Mode `execute` wrapper (`{ code }`), and each nested `tools.<name>()`
  call re-enters `tool.execute.before` under its own name. The completion gate
  judged the wrapper itself as an opaque, non-read-only tool, so once a task
  reached `tests_run` it denied every plugin call — including the
  `update_task_status` remedy its own message prescribes and the exempt
  `check_gate_status` — and the task could never leave the gate. The PR author
  reported this on a live session (11 consecutive
  `TASK_COMPLETION_GATE_VIOLATION` denials for one task over about 11 hours);
  that observation is not reproducible from the repository.
- The wrapper call that the v2 adapter marked (`execute` with a string `code`
  program) now passes the completion gate. Each nested `tools.<name>()` call is
  still gated under its own name, so hooked mutating tools remain blocked while
  a task awaits completion. An `execute` call the adapter did not mark stays
  gated. Limits: the mark is not proof of provenance (a plugin or MCP tool that
  is also named `execute` and takes a string `code` is marked too), and the gate
  does not inspect the program, so sandbox effects no

## Host contract drift (v2): vendored types and corpus refreshed to @opencode/plugin@2.3.0

The vendored OpenCode 2 plugin types (`src/host/v2/types.ts`) and the committed
host-contract corpus (`tests/fixtures/host/expected-structure-v2.json`) were pinned to
`@opencode/plugin@2.0.26` while the published package advanced to 2.3.0; the weekly
`host-contract-check` reported structural drift and auto-filed #3732 (and #3552 at the
2.2.5 snapshot). Both now pin 2.3.0 and the weekly check reports `STRUCTURE_MATCH`.

The vendored surface now carries the 2.1–2.3 additions, compiler-verified against the
tagged tarballs (the surfaces the adapter and type-probe cover): `Context.credential` (activate), `Context.experimental` (terminal read,
stateless generate, artifact) and the deprecated top-level `Context.generate`;
`SessionRequestMessage` (readonly nullable-text content, wired into the context event);
`SessionCompactionResult.native` (replacing the providerState era); the
`SessionModelResolve` / `SessionIdle` / fork hook payload families with a payload-typed
session hook registration; the paginated `session.list` (`{data, cursor}`) and the
deprecated `session.instructions` entries; 2.3.0 `AgentEditor` readonly signatures; and
the 2.3.0 permission `assert` input (optional agent/save/metadata/source, readonly
arrays).

Behavior: types-only for the adapter except one contract-alignment change — the v2
guidance context hook now replaces message elements instead of mutating the host's
message objects in place when writing transformed text parts back (the published
content array is readonly at 2.3.0; the event array itself is still rewritten in place,
so guidance delivery is unchanged).

New surfaces are documented per-hook in `docs/host/v2-hook-inventory.md` with the
adoption owner (#3642); no new hook is adopted at runtime in this change.

---

## What changed

- **PR_FEEDBACK verification rejections stop consuming gate state** (#3644 AC1): a
  `swarm-pr-feedback:verification` request whose lanes own an item not in the
  requested inventory (or doubly-claim an item) is now rejected by a request-pure
  shape check that runs BEFORE any state mutation — before PR_FEEDBACK activation on
  a fresh session and before the append-only inventory declaration on an active one.
  Previously the typo'd inventory was persisted first, so the corrected retry was
  wedged by the append-only rule ("may not be removed or renamed"). The stateful
  predicates (duplicate batch id, capacity, cross-batch ownership) are unchanged.
- **Unlaunchable base/micro lane agents are refused before activation** (#3644 AC2):
  base and micro admission now runs the same `validateLaneAgent` launchability probe
  the lane launcher uses (including the bare-canonical-role registry refusal on
  prefixed-only multi-swarm hosts), so such requests no longer activate the workflow
  and bind/record state before launch rejects them. The set of rejected requests is
  unchanged — only the durable-state consumption moves.
- **stage-b-test lanes carry the verdict-mandate suspension clause** (#3645): the
  fourth ordered PR-feedback gate now gets the same controller-authored PROTOCOL
  SELECTION clause the other four gates have, suspending the test_engineer prompt's
  task-keyed `[TESTED]` "STRUCTURED VERDICT LINE" mandate in favor of the gate's
  item-keyed `[STAGE-B-TEST] | <item_id> | PASS` settlement rows — closing the same
  conflict class that voided reviewer lanes before the clause mechanism existed.

- **Both #3752 residual paths are fixed in this PR** (maintainer decision, option
  (b)): a verification dispatch rejected for a STATEFUL reason after an inventory
  amendment (duplicate batch id, capacity after prune, cross-batch exclusivity)
  no longer persists the amendment — the dispatch path runs
  `declareAndEnforcePrFeedbackVerification`, a single-bind/single-write
  transaction, so the corrected retry is never wedged; and every recognized
  PR_

# Redaction fill-tolerance and five JWT shapes at both redaction sites; win32 probe/weak-executor TTL

## What

- Closes #3730: the shell-audit redaction site (`redactShellCommand`) gains the
  display site's Cf/DI condensed-union bare-token sweep — a zero-width byte
  (e.g. U+200B, U+070F, U+1160, U+FE0F) inside ANY bare credential token (jwt,
  sk-, ghp_, AKIA, xoxb-, AIza, gsk_, …) can no longer split it past redaction.
  Benign text keeps its invisible bytes byte-identical (condensation exists
  only in the matching view).
- Closes #3736 claim 1: the shared JWS scanner (`src/utils/jws-redaction.ts`)
  is widened at BOTH redaction sites for five previously-leaking shapes —
  n-part JWE absorption (never across an adjacent eyJ header; the empty
  encrypted-key dir-JWE is covered when its IV segment passes the token-like
  check — spec-length IVs of 16+ chars), unsigned 2-segment tokens with any
  ≥1-char payload (e30/bnVsbA/Ingi), standard-base64 `+ / =` dotted headers
  whose standard-alphabet header is 40+ chars (bare, `key=` assignment, and
  `=`/`==`-padded placements), `_eyJ` underscore boundaries, and ≥1-char
  signatures.
- Known bounds (documented residuals, tracked for a follow-up): an empty-key
  JWE whose IV segment fails the token-like check (the segment lacks the
  uppercase/mixed-case/digit or length-16 composition the heuristic requires
  — e.g. an all-lowercase or all-digit IV shorter than 16 chars, or any IV
  shorter than 8 chars) stays fully visible (pre-existing — base is
  byte-identical); a standard-alphabet token whose header is 13-39 chars
  (e.g. the canonical 36-char HS256 header with `+`/`/`/`=` later segments)
  is not covered by the 40+ generic arm and can stay visible (real JWTs are
  base64url, so reach is limited); a dot-glued standard-base64 token directly
  after an eyJ token can keep its final segments visible (the absorption loop
  stops and the overlapping generic span is dropped); a mixed-case ≥8-char
  English tail directly appended to a token absorbs; an all-lowercase
  <16-char ciphertext tail stays visible; the generic arm can over-redact a
  benign dotted identifier whose first run is 40+ chars of `[A-Za-z0-9+/]`
  followed by 20+/10+ char segments (and `/swarm close` re-applies current
  policy when re-archiving shell-audit lines, so such identifiers logged
  under the previous policy may be redacted in the archived copy).
- Closes #3736 claim 2: every failed/unavailable win32 runner-probe result is
  now TTL-bounded (`runnerProbeFailureTtlMs()`, env
  `SWARM_SANDBOX_RUNNER_PROBE_FAILURE_TTL_MS`, default 60 s, mirroring
  `executorFailureTtlMs()`) so installing or replacing the runner binary is
  recoverable, and `getExecutor()` re-creates a WEAK executor after the
  executor TTL instead of pinning the PowerShell fallback for the process
  lifetime. Recovery bound: ≤ probe TTL + executor TTL + next-caller delay
  (both default 60 s) — this bounded recovery covers the weak-executor path;
  a `strength === 'none'` executor and the capability-probe/assessment
  memoization still pin as before (pre-existing; tracked). The #2475
  downgrade warnings are now bounded per attempt/reconstruction while broken
  (one warn per failed probe attempt plus one per weak-executor
  reconstruction; the two TTLs are independently configurable and other
  callers may probe between reconstructions, so the combined cadence is the
  sum of those two bounded rates — the bounded re-probe cadence IS the
  recovery mechanism) instead of once per process.
- Glued compositions (`sk-abc-<JWT>`) now select the leftmost-longest family
  span at BOTH sites (disclosed behavior change: the old shell pre-pass
  labeled them jwt; the new span is strictly more redaction).
- Same-class siblings outside this change's surfaces (probe-verified /
  source-traced, recorded for follow-up #3743): the memory-storage secret
  scanner (`src/memory/redaction.ts` findSecrets) has the zw-split gap;

# Unclaimed `.swarm/` directories get a lifecycle

## What

The retention sweep only ever reclaimed the `.swarm/` families it hardcoded,
and blocked every other delete under `.swarm/` — so any directory a subagent
wrote outside that closed set had no lifecycle at all and no supported command
could reclaim it. One production project had 140 MB of its 166 MB `.swarm/`
sitting in `.swarm/review-sandbox` and `.swarm/review-mut`, written by reviewer
subagents and reclaimable by nothing.

Directories immediately under `.swarm/` now have three tiers of ownership:

1. **Tier 1 — hardcoded preserve allowlist.** Swarm's own state (database and
   sidecars, memory, evidence, plan store, knowledge, session/summary state,
   every retention family root, skill stores, locks, quarantine, …) is never
   pruned by the catch-all, whatever its age.
2. **Tier 2 — owner manifests.** `.swarm/retention.d/<owner>.json`:
   `{ "owner": "reviewer", "preserve": ["review-sandbox"], "maxAgeDays": 90 }`.
   One file per owner and one writer each, so there is no shared file to merge
   and no cross-agent edit surface — a single shared config key would turn
   every new scratch owner into a conflict in one file. A claim is a lease, not
   a permanent exemption: the claim SETS the directory's horizon to its
   `maxAgeDays` (longer or shorter than the 30-day default), and past it the
   directory becomes reclaimable again, because a claim that never expires
   would recreate the very defect this fixes. A malformed, ambiguous, or unreadable manifest
   refuses the **whole** sweep (fail closed) and names the file and the reason.
3. **Tier 3 — catch-all.** An unclaimed directory is pruned only when it is a
   real directory (never a symlink), has no `.preserve` marker, contains no
   future-dated entries, and all of its content is older than its horizon
   (30 days by default, or the owning manifest's `maxAgeDays`). The pass
   refuses to run when `.swarm/retention.log` is a link, is not a regular file,
   or cannot be inspected, so a prune is not started against a log it cannot
   record to (a permission failure on a regular log still surfaces only after
   the deletes, in `result.errors`); after the deletes, every pruned path is appended to the
   log as `<ISO-8601> pruned <path> age=<days> size=<bytes>` (control characters
   in a name are escaped), and the log itself is compacted to its newest
   256 KiB.

`retention.dry_run` (`runRetentionSweep({ dryRun: true })`) keeps its existing
count-and-report behaviour and now also populates `result.explained` with every
planned prune (path, age, size, owning manifest) and writes that list to the
debug log (visible only with `OPENCODE_SWARM_DEBUG=1`), which is how an operator previews what the catch-all would remove
before enabling it. It deletes nothing: no family file and no directory.

Containment has three layers. The catch-all refuses to run at all when `.swarm`
is itself a link (a `.swarm` linked to the project root would otherwise make
`.git` and `src` look like unclaimed children). Each candidate must be a real
directory, not a link. And each candidate is `realpath`-ed and required to be an
immediate child of the `realpath`-ed `.swarm` root immediately before deletion;
this narrows, but cannot close, the window in which a parent could be swapped
for a link, and that window needs write access to `.swarm`.

## Why

An unbounded, unreclaimable directory family is a disk-exhaustion defect with
no operator remedy: the shell guardrails refuse an unsanctioned recursive
delete, and the sweep refused every path it had not been taught. The three
tiers restore the missing lifecycle without weakening either safety property
that caused the refusal — swarm's own state stays untouchable, and an
ownership claim that cannot be parsed stops the sweep rather than being
treated as permission to delete.

## Migration

No config key and no API removal, but **this release deletes data on upgrade**

# First-turn bundled-skill ordering, full-auto resume mode/CAS, and git-init spawn diagnostics

## What changed

- **First-turn bundled-skill ordering (#3364):** the deferred bundled-skill
  materialization now pre-registers a completion handle at post-resolution-task
  enqueue time, and a gate composed FIRST in the chat messages transform awaits
  it (single 15 s budget) before the first turn proceeds. A fresh project's
  first architect MODE self-load can no longer race the copy — measured in
  19/19 live observations (ADR-0003 measurement of record, windows
  ~0.4–4.2 s) with the first turn arriving before the copy finished. **Known
  bound (disclosed; owner confirmation pending — the plan-approval question
  went unanswered 2026-11-14, adopted under the session's standing work
  authorization):** three escapes keep today's
  fail-open behavior for that turn (command-path sync backstop intact): a copy
  slower than the 15 s budget, a genuinely failed sync, and registration refusal
  at the internal 8-root cap (practically unreachable — one project root per
  plugin process). The first turn of ANY agent in the project pays the single
  wait; later turns are immediate.
- **Full-Auto resume mode + CAS (#3106):** `/swarm full-auto resume` now
  re-derives the armed mode from live config (`full_auto.mode`, defaulting to
  `supervised`) instead of re-arming the paused-time mode — a post-pause config
  tightening is in force for the resumed run. BEHAVIOR CHANGE (disclosed,
  owner decision at the PR): the parsed config ALWAYS materializes
  `full_auto.mode` (schema default `supervised`), so the config value —
  explicit or defaulted — always wins on resume: a per-run `on strict`
  override pauses and resumes as `supervised` under a default config (the
  pre-fix behavior kept the paused-time mode). A post-pause config LOOSENING
  also applies. The raw-config hybrid (override survives unless the config
  explicitly sets a mode) is the recorded owner follow-up option. Resume also arms through an expected-pauseGeneration CAS under the state
  lock: a second process aborting, disarming, or re-pausing the run inside the
  check-then-arm window is refused with state- and reason-conditional
  guidance instead of being silently resurrected (an infrastructure re-pause
  is directed to `retry-oversight`; a non-infrastructure re-pause names the
  reason and directs to `off` then `on`; an abort or disarm directs to
  re-enable with `on`).
- **git-init harness diagnostics (#3691):** the delegation-gate test harness's
  `initProject` moved to `tests/helpers/git-init-project.ts` and now throws with
  `result.error`/`status=`/`signal=` plus a bounded stderr tail — the empty
  `Error: ` CI failure class (run 43380165115) is diagnosable from the log line.

## Why

Issue #3364 measured the first-turn window on a real host (16/16 runs in the
issue's own probe; the ADR-0003 measurement of record cited above is 19/19,
windows ~0.4–4.2 s); nothing
ordered the architect's MODE self-load read after the deferred copy, so
`SKILL_LOAD_FAILED` was reachable by timing luck. Issue #3106 carried two
verified findings from the PR #3091 review (paused-time mode re-arm asymmetry
with `on`, and the non-atomic check-then-arm window that resurrects terminal
state). Issue #3691 recorded the second episode of the delegation-gate
git-init flake with an undiagnosable empty error.

## Boundaries

- The gate adds NO awaited I/O on the plugin-init path (repro-704 stays green);
  the wait happens at first-turn time only.
- The CAS is opt-in: only the resume command passes the expected generation;
  `on` and the intercept hooks keep the unconditional arm.
- v2 hosts share the fix through the same v1 messages-transform chain — no
  separate v2 wiring. On v2 the gate's 15 s budget runs inside the 30 s
  guidance-chain budget (V2_GUIDANCE_CHAIN_TIMEOUT_MS): only the disclosed
  >15 s copy escape can consume it, and chain exhaustion restores the
